title: Adaptive matrix replay and targeted eval harness for post-incident regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: A recent customer-facing incident revealed a subtle interaction between a runtime config mutation (long-prefix KV TTL reduction) and a model variant change that produced a quality regression only under a narrow sequence-length distribution. Root cause analysis showed our existing smoke evals and golden snapshots missed the combination of config+model because we only replay single-dimension traces (either config or model) rather than combinatorial intersections.

Goal: Build an adaptive 'matrix' replay harness that can: (1) automatically synthesize targeted evaluation cases from incident traces by enumerating a bounded set of model/config axes, (2) prioritize test candidates by signal-to-noise (delta on quality metrics), (3) generate synthetic augmentations to increase coverage of rare sequence-length / tokenization edge-cases, and (4) push failing candidates into an automated regression test set and a canary gate for future rollouts.

Scope: MVP covers config axes (KV TTL, batching window, prefix caching toggles, quantization flags) and model axes (model family, quantized variant, max-seq delta). Integrations: incident-runbook -> replay generator, eval pipeline -> scorer (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim), console -> regression dashboard, and PR automation that auto-creates regression test PRs for infra tests. Exclusions: full end-to-end user traffic shadowing and full retraining of models.

Implementation approach:
- Spike: collect a representative set of incident traces and produce a small combinatorial matrix (bounded by heuristics) to avoid explosion.
- Smart sampling: apply importance sampling to select the top-K matrix cells most likely to reveal regression (based on tokenization deltas, sequence length, and prompt templates).
- Augmenter: for low-frequency cells, apply deterministic augmentations (prefix padding, token aliasing) to stress tokenization/kv interactions.
- Evaluation harness: replay requests deterministically through runtime with instrumentation to capture per-token logits and final outputs; compare against golden oracle and existing baseline metrics.
- Automation: failing cells are recorded to a 'regression bank' that can seed synthetic smoke tests and a canary check during config/model rollouts.

Deliverables: replay harness (go + python), sampling heuristics, augmentation library, dashboard widgets for 'matrix heatmap', automation to file regression PRs, and a short runbook for on-call triage.

Risks: combinatorial explosion, false positives due to nondeterministic model outputs, performance cost for running large matrix replays. Mitigations: bounded heuristics, random-seed normalization, and cost budget gating with async replays for low-priority cells.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can take an incident trace and produce a bounded matrix (<=200 cells) covering config+model axes
Top-20 prioritized cells reproduce the customer-visible regression locally in >=1 test run
Generated failing cells are automatically added to the regression bank with metadata (trace id, axis values, diff metrics)
Console shows a matrix heatmap for a replay with clickable cells linking to repro artifacts and logs
Automation opens a draft PR with test scaffolding for infra tests when a regression cell is persistent across 3 runs
